claim: The Mangart Saddle road reaches 2,067 m, runs 23.9 km from Bovec via Log pod Mangartom and Strmec na Predelu, is fully paved but narrow with five unlit rock tunnels and gradients up to 23% with no edge protection on big drops.
quote: It's the highest-lying road in the country. The route spans 23.9km from Bovec... 5 unlit tunnels carved into bedrock... brutally steep parts (up to 23%)... no protections on sections with drops reaching hundreds of meters.

claim: The Mangart Saddle is about 45 minutes from Bovec, climbs 980 m in under 12 km with five tunnels, costs about €10 toll, and is normally open May–November.
quote: The Mangart Saddle is located just 45 minutes from Bovec. In less than 12 km, this road climbs 980 meters and winds its way through five tunnels carved out of the rock... The toll to continue is €10 (in 2025).

claim: The Vršič Pass (Route 206) at 1,611 m connects Kranjska Gora and Bovec with 50 hairpins (24 north, 26 south), is fully asphalted with cobblestone switchbacks for traction, and typically opens early May after winter closure.
quote: Vršič is the highest mountain pass in Slovenia, with an elevation of 1,611 metres... The winding road has a total of 50 serpentines, 24 on the Kranjska Gora side and 26 on the Trenta side.

claim: The Predel/Predil Pass at 1,156 m crosses from Bovec to Cave del Predil/Tarvisio in Italy in three stages totalling 30 km, is wider and lower than Vršič, open year-round, and passes the Napoleonic-era stone lion monument.
quote: The Predel Pass is another winding high-altitude road, although slightly lower and wider than the Vrsic Pass. The Predel pass is open all year... Bovec to Strmec na Predelu (14 km), Strmec na Predelu to Predel Pass (3 km), and Predel Pass to Tarvisio (13 km).

claim: Kolovrat is a Julian Prealp ridge straddling the Slovenia–Italy border west of Tolmin and southeast of Kobarid, reaching 1,115 m with panoramic views over the Veneto plain and Soča Valley.
quote: Kolovrat is a mountain ridge of the Julian Prealps on the border between Slovenia and Italy, west of Tolmin and southeast of Kobarid.

claim: Drive Kobarid → Idrsko → Livek (5 km) → Livške Ravne (4 km), then 3 km along the ridge to the Kolovrat Outdoor Museum parking; the route is paved but narrow and winding and the WWI open-air museum is free.
quote: On the road from Kobarid towards Tolmin, in the settlement of Idrsko, turn towards the village of Livek (5 km), then turn left towards Livške Ravne (4 km)... continue for 3 kilometers along the ridge of Kolovrat to the smaller parking site.

claim: Robidišče is Slovenia's westernmost settlement, reached via Breginj → Borjana → Podbela → Napoleon Bridge, characterised by Venetian-Slovenian stone architecture with outer stairways and wooden 'ganks'.
quote: Robidišče lies on the western edge of Slovenia, enclosed by the state border from the north, west and south... To reach Robidišče you need to take the road for Breginj, and in Borjana you take a turn for Podbela, then pass the village of Podbela, pass the Napoleon Bridge and continue to Robidišče.

claim: Robidišče sits in the Breginjski Kot among 13 villages along the crystal-clear Nadiža River, with hike-up viewpoints reaching toward Resia, the Soča and the Adriatic, and gravity bike routes into Italian Benečija.
quote: Robidišče is a perfect starting point to discover the rolling hills of Venetian Slovenia, cycling to scenic viewpoints, and continuing along the ridges of Benečija to the village of Prosnid.

claim: Cividale del Friuli sits roughly 21 km / 17 miles from Kobarid, about a 29-minute drive across the Stupizza/Robič border crossing.
quote: The driving distance between Cividale del Friuli and Kobarid is 17 miles, taking approximately 29 minutes to drive.

claim: Cividale del Friuli is UNESCO-listed (since 2011) with the Lombard Tempietto, Piazza del Duomo, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta and Christian Museum; the Natisone Valleys hold stone-house hamlets, 15th-century churches and Slovene-Italian cultural roots.
quote: Cividale del Friuli, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2011, boasts attractions such as Piazza del Duomo, the Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, the Christian Museum, and the Town Hall with the statue of Julius Caesar.

claim: The Natisone/Nadiža is a 60-km river crossing the Slovenia–Italy border through villages such as Pulfero and San Pietro al Natisone, providing the scenic valley road link to Cividale.
quote: The Natisone (also known as Nadiža in Slovene) is a 60-kilometre river in Slovenia and Italy.

claim: Stol (1,673 m) is the highest Slovenian peak on the long Julian Alps ridge above Breginj, an exceptional viewpoint reaching from the Adriatic to the central Julian Alps, recognisable by its summit transmitter; access is by road from Kobarid to Breginj then on foot.
quote: Stol is the highest Slovenian peak in the longest ridge of the Julian Alps and is an exceptional viewpoint from which you can see from the sea to the central Julian Alps. It is recognizable from afar due to the transmitter standing on its summit.

claim: Drežnica sits at around 560 m on a plateau under Mt Krn directly above Kobarid, famed for the Sacred Heart church (consecrated 1912) that survived WWI, an ancient pagan-rooted carnival, and as a premier paragliding launch site.
quote: The picturesque Drežnica lies at an altitude of about 560 meters, and Drežnica is especially popular with paragliders – its position above the Soča valley makes it possible to sail with all four winds.

claim: Drežniške Ravne, together with Drežnica, Koseč, Jezerca and Magozd, forms a cluster of mountain hamlets on a small plateau above the Soča at the foot of Mt Krn with around 565 inhabitants between them.
quote: Drežniške Ravne is a settlement in the Municipality of Kobarid in the Littoral region of Slovenia, and it is located above the Soča River on a small plateau under Mount Krn.

claim: Bovec town centre offers a small brewpub brewing on premises and easy walks/cycles to Slap Boka (roadside waterfall) and Slap Virje (forest pool waterfall) within 5–10 minutes of the square.
quote: Slap Boka is a must and very easy to see as it's along the main road just outside Bovec centre. Slap Virje is another waterfall within walking or biking distance from the centre.

claim: Most na Soči sits 5 km south of Tolmin on a turquoise reservoir lake at the Soča–Idrijca confluence, with lakeside paths, viewpoint at St Mary's church, archaeological museum, boat rides and SUP/kayak rentals.
quote: Most na Soči... The settlement is located 5km south of Tolmin... the village sits on a beautiful aquamarine lake – an artificial lake at the confluence of the Soča and Idrijca Rivers.

claim: The Kobarid Historical Trail is a 5 km, ~3-hour loop from the town centre passing the Italian Charnel House on Gradič hill, Tonocov grad Roman remains, Italian WWI defensive lines, the Soča gorge, the Napoleon Bridge and Kozjak Waterfall.
quote: The Kobarid Historical Trail leads visitors to places in the surroundings of Kobarid where there are significant historical, cultural, and natural points of interest. It is 5 kilometres long and it takes 3 hours.

claim: The Kobarid Museum (founded 1990, Council of Europe Museum Prize 1993) sits just off Kobarid's main square in a former Italian military court building and covers the static Isonzo/Soča Front and the Caporetto breakthrough of October 1917.
quote: The Kobarid Museum was established in 1990 in the Slovene town Kobarid (called Karfreit when part of the Austro-Hungarian empire, and Caporetto under the Italians) near the Italian border, and won the prestigious Council of Europe Museum Prize in 1993.
